import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Survival Rate by Class
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
survival_by_class = data.groupby('pclass')['survived'].mean()
survival_by_class.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax1, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black')
ax1.set_title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class')
ax1.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
ax1.set_xticklabels(['1st', '2nd', '3rd'], rotation=0)
ax1.set_ylim([0, 1])

# 2. Survival Rate by Sex
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
survival_by_sex = data.groupby('sex')['survived'].mean()
survival_by_sex.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax2, color=['lightcoral', 'skyblue'], edgecolor='black')
ax2.set_title('Survival Rate by Sex', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Sex')
ax2.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
ax2.set_xticklabels(['Female', 'Male'], rotation=0)
ax2.set_ylim([0, 1])

# 3. Age Distribution by Survival
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
data_clean = data.dropna(subset=['age'])
survived_ages = data_clean[data_clean['survived'] == 1]['age']
died_ages = data_clean[data_clean['survived'] == 0]['age']
ax3.hist([survived_ages, died_ages], bins=20, label=['Survived', 'Died'], 
         color=['green', 'red'], alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_title('Age Distribution by Survival', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Age')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.legend()

# 4. Survival Count
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
survival_counts = data['survived'].value_counts()
ax4.pie(survival_counts, labels=['Died', 'Survived'], autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=['#ff6b6b', '#51cf66'], startangle=90)
ax4.set_title('Overall Survival Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Fare Distribution by Class
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
for pclass in sorted(data['pclass'].unique()):
    class_data = data[data['pclass'] == pclass]['fare']
    ax5.hist(class_data, alpha=0.6, label=f'Class {pclass}', bins=20, edgecolor='black')
ax5.set_title('Fare Distribution by Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Fare')
ax5.set_ylabel('Count')
ax5.legend()

# 6. Survival by Embark Town
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
embark_survival = data.groupby('embark_town')['survived'].mean().sort_values()
embark_survival.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax6, color='teal', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_title('Survival Rate by Embarkation Town', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Survival Rate')
ax6.set_ylabel('Embarkation Town')
ax6.set_xlim([0, 1])

# 7. Family Size vs Survival
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
data['family_size'] = data['sibsp'] + data['parch']
family_survival = data.groupby('family_size')['survived'].mean()
family_survival.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax7, color='orange', edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_title('Survival Rate by Family Size', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Family Size')
ax7.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
ax7.set_ylim([0, 1])

# 8. Heatmap of Survival by Class and Sex
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
survival_matrix = data.pivot_table(values='survived', index='sex', columns='pclass', aggfunc='mean')
sns.heatmap(survival_matrix, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='RdYlGn', ax=ax8, 
            cbar_kws={'label': 'Survival Rate'}, vmin=0, vmax=1)
ax8.set_title('Survival Rate Heatmap: Sex vs Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Passenger Class')
ax8.set_ylabel('Sex')

# 9. Alone vs Not Alone Survival
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
alone_survival = data.groupby('alone')['survived'].mean()
alone_survival.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax9, color=['mediumpurple', 'gold'], edgecolor='black')
ax9.set_title('Survival Rate: Alone vs With Family', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax9.set_xlabel('Traveling Status')
ax9.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
ax9.set_xticklabels(['With Family', 'Alone'], rotation=0)
ax9.set_ylim([0, 1])

plt.suptitle('Titanic Dataset: Comprehensive Survival Analysis', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
